title: Agent Builder's Playbook — Oct 9, 2026
intro: Guardrails and evals are the common thread: make failing hooks block, and verify graders before trusting their scores.

cards.title: Route each coding task to the cheapest model that clears it
cards.problem: Running every coding-agent task on your top model inflates daily spend without speeding anyone up.
cards.apply: Label your recurring agent tasks by difficulty, assign each label a model tier, and set a daily budget per team. Review the mapping weekly against rework rates.
cards.result: LegalOn reports a 65% cut in estimated daily Codex cost with development speed unchanged.

evidence.note: LegalOn states the 65% figure for its own estimated daily Codex costs.

cards.title: Bind tools to skills so they load only when the skill does
cards.problem: A large skill library plus every tool schema in context crowds out the task and confuses tool selection.
cards.apply: Declare each skill's tools alongside the skill, pin the skills a run needs at start, and reload skills mid-thread instead of preloading all of them.
cards.result: Context stays focused on the active task even as the skill repository grows.

evidence.note: Deep Agents now supports binding tools to skills, runtime pinning, and mid-thread reload.

cards.title: Make guardrail hooks block the action when they fail
cards.problem: A policy hook that crashes, times out, or exits unexpectedly silently lets the risky action through.
cards.apply: Set `onFailure: "block"` on command and HTTP hooks that enforce policy, and keep the default pass-through only for advisory hooks. Test by killing the hook process.
cards.result: A broken guardrail now stops the action instead of disabling itself unnoticed.

evidence.note: claude-code v2.1.295 adds onFailure: "block" for command and HTTP hooks.

cards.title: Audit your verifier before reading a score change as capability
cards.problem: A rising eval or reward score may reflect a change in the verifier, not in the agent.
cards.apply: Freeze the verifier version per comparison, and re-score a fixed sample of past agent traces whenever you change it. Treat any score shift that appears on identical traces as verifier drift.
cards.result: Score changes you report to your team trace to the agent, not the grader.

evidence.note: TRACE argues verifier scores serve as both benchmark metrics and training rewards, so verifier changes can masquerade as capability changes.

cards.title: Review AGENTS.md and rule files like code before agents read them
cards.problem: Community-shared rule files can steer a coding agent into installing hallucinated or attacker-registered packages.
cards.apply: Pin rule files to reviewed commits, diff them on every update, and require the agent to check any new dependency against an allowlist or lockfile before installing.
cards.result: Injected rule-file instructions can no longer add a dependency without a human-visible change.

evidence.note: The paper studies package hallucination attacks delivered through prompt injection in AGENTS.md and .cursorrules-style files.

cards.title: Seed your red-team harness with attacks your defenses already blocked
cards.problem: Static test suites for a protective layer go stale as soon as attackers vary their payloads.
cards.apply: Run models inside a sandboxed harness that takes blocked requests from your logs, has the model mutate them, and reports which variants get through.
cards.result: Cloudflare reports this surfaces WAF bypasses from variants of attacks it already blocks, before attackers find them.

evidence.note: Cloudflare describes using blocked attacks as starting points for models to generate and refine WAF-probing variants.
